newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to wind up loss-making Channel ferry firm.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to wind up loss-making Channel ferry firm.

text.p: The Belgian government said on Friday its loss-making, state-owned Channel ferry operator RTM/RMT would be wound up in 1999, leaving the Ramsgate to Ostend route to be run by Australia's Holyman Ltd and Sally Lines, a unit of Finland's Silja Oy.

RTM/RMT, hit by competition from other Channel ferry operators and the Channel Tunnel, has lost money every year since 1992 and has accumulated debts of 12 billion Belgian francs ($384.7 million). The government forecasts 1996's loss will be around three billion Belgian francs.
Earlier this year the government appointed a "crisis manager" to run the company while a search for a partner or possible buyer was organised.
It was agreed the route could only be made profitable by replacing RTM/RMT's three ageing vessels and one more modern "jumbo" ferry, the Prins Filip, by high speed catamarans.
Silja Oy said separately on Friday that Holyman Sally would operate two catamarans, carrying 674 passengers and 180 private cars, which would halve the journey time between the ports.
In a statement, the government said however that until 1999 the Ramsgate-Ostend route would be run on a pool basis by both RTM/RMT and Holyman Sally.

RTM/RMT would likely lose a further 1.8 and 1.6 billion Belgian francs in 1997 and 1998, the government said, adding it hoped the losses could be covered in part by the sale of its ships and other assets.
"Additional options concerning (RTM/RMT's) freight activities and the use of the Prins Filip continue to be studied," the government said.
